interview.q: What is the benefit of utility-first CSS?
interview.answer: It co-locates styling with markup and avoids naming and specificity issues.

interview.q: What is the downside of utility-first CSS?
interview.answer: Markup becomes verbose and learning the class names takes time.

interview.q: What is the difference between reset and normalize?
interview.answer: Reset wipes defaults; normalize keeps them consistent and accessible.

interview.q: How do you split CSS files?

interview.q: What is the difference between CSS modules and shadow DOM?
interview.answer: CSS modules scope at build time; shadow DOM scopes at runtime with full encapsulation.
